title: Dearness Allowance: Understanding Your DA Hike Calculation Formula
description: Dearness Allowance (DA) is a crucial component of salary and pension for central government employees and pensioners, designed to offset inflation's impact. T.

faq.q: What is the difference between Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR)?
faq.a: DA is paid to serving central government employees, while DR is paid to central government pensioners. Both serve the same purpose of compensating for inflation.
DA/DR is typically revised twice a year, effective from January 1st and July 1st. The announcements are usually made a few months after these effective dates.
Yes, Dearness Allowance is fully taxable. It is added to your basic salary to calculate your gross income, which is then subject to income tax as per the prevailing slabs.

faq.q: Who is eligible for Dearness Allowance?
faq.a: Central government employees and pensioners are eligible for Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR), respectively. Some state governments and public sector undertakings also provide similar allowances.

While the core principle remains, the specific constant values or base year for the AICPI-IW in the formula can be updated by Pay Commissions or government directives, as seen with the shift from earlier pay commissions to the 7th Pay Commission.

faq.q: What is the All-India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (AICPI-IW)?
faq.a: AICPI-IW is a key economic indicator published by the Labour Bureau that measures the average change in prices of a basket of goods and services consumed by industrial workers, reflecting inflation.
